# Type Assertion & Type Switch in Go

When working with interfaces, we often need to retrieve the underlying concrete type. Go provides **type assertion** and **type switch** for this purpose.

## Type Assertion: `x.(T)`

```go
var i interface{} = "hello"
s := i.(string)  // panics if wrong type!
fmt.Println(s)   // hello
```

## Comma-Ok Pattern

```go
var i interface{} = "hello"

s, ok := i.(string)
fmt.Println(s, ok) // hello true

n, ok := i.(int)
fmt.Println(n, ok) // 0 false — no panic!
```

## Type Switch

```go
func describe(i interface{}) string {
    switch v := i.(type) {
    case int:    return fmt.Sprintf("int: %d", v)
    case string: return fmt.Sprintf("string: %q", v)
    case bool:   return fmt.Sprintf("bool: %v", v)
    case nil:    return "nil"
    default:     return fmt.Sprintf("unknown: %T", v)
    }
}
```

## Practical Error Handling

```go
func handleError(err error) {
    switch e := err.(type) {
    case *ValidationError:
        fmt.Printf("Field %s: %s\n", e.Field, e.Message)
    case *NotFoundError:
        fmt.Printf("%s not found\n", e.Resource)
    default:
        fmt.Printf("Unknown error: %v\n", err)
    }
}
```

quiz.question_id: Apa beda utama antara `i.(string)` dan `i.(int)` saat `i` menyimpan string?
quiz.question_en: What is the main difference between `i.(string)` and `i.(int)` when `i` stores a string?
options_id: Keduanya error kompilasi karena interface tidak bisa di-assert
Yang pertama berhasil, yang kedua panic saat runtime
Keduanya mengembalikan zero value jika tipe salah
options_en: Both are compile errors because interfaces cannot be asserted
The first succeeds, the second panics at runtime
Both return zero values when the type is wrong
Both perform automatic conversions

quiz.question_id: Apa hasil dari `n, ok := i.(int)` jika `i` berisi string?
quiz.question_en: What is the result of `n, ok := i.(int)` if `i` contains a string?
options_en: `n` becomes a random value and `ok` is false
`n` becomes `nil` and `ok` is false
`n` becomes `0` and `ok` is false
The program panics before assignment

quiz.question_id: Mengapa comma-ok pattern lebih aman untuk data dengan tipe dinamis?
quiz.question_en: Why is the comma-ok pattern safer for dynamically typed data?
options_id: Karena memberi sinyal kegagalan tanpa panic
options_en: Because it makes type assertions faster
Because it signals failure without panicking
Because it turns the interface into a pointer
Because it forces all cases to be handled

quiz.question_id: Dalam `switch v := i.(type)`, apa tipe dari `v` di dalam `case []int:`?
quiz.question_en: In `switch v := i.(type)`, what is the type of `v` inside `case []int:`?
options_en: It remains `interface{}`
A string containing the type name
`[]int`
A pointer to `[]int`

quiz.question_id: Kapan type switch lebih tepat daripada beberapa direct assertion terpisah?
quiz.question_en: When is a type switch more appropriate than several separate direct assertions?
options_id: Ketika hanya ada satu tipe pasti
Ketika perlu membedakan banyak kemungkinan tipe dengan cabang yang berbeda
options_en: When there is only one guaranteed type
When you need to distinguish among many possible types with different branches
When you want to avoid all interfaces
Only when the value is nil

quiz.question_id: Apa yang ditangani oleh `case nil` dalam type switch?
quiz.question_en: What does `case nil` handle in a type switch?
options_id: Semua interface yang berisi typed nil pointer
Hanya nilai interface yang benar-benar nil
Semua zero value dari tipe apa pun
options_en: All interfaces that contain typed nil pointers
Only an interface value that is truly nil
All zero values of any type
Only nil struct pointers

quiz.question_id: Pada contoh `describeShape`, apa yang terjadi jika ditambahkan tipe `Hexagon` yang mengimplementasikan `Shape` tetapi tidak punya case khusus?
quiz.question_en: In the `describeShape` example, what happens if a `Hexagon` type is added that implements `Shape` but has no dedicated case?
options_id: Compile error sampai case baru ditambahkan
options_en: A compile error occurs until a new case is added
The program panics when the switch runs
The value falls into the `default` case
The value is automatically treated as `Circle`

quiz.question_id: Apa keuntungan type switch untuk error seperti `switch e := err.(type)`?
quiz.question_en: What is the advantage of a type switch for errors such as `switch e := err.(type)`?
options_id: Kita bisa menangani tiap tipe error konkret dan mengakses field atau method yang relevan
options_en: The error is converted into a string
We can handle each concrete error type and access relevant fields or methods
Error wrapping is automatically removed
All errors are treated the same

quiz.question_id: Apa yang dibuktikan oleh fungsi `safeGetRadius(s Shape) (float64, bool)`?
quiz.question_en: What does the function `safeGetRadius(s Shape) (float64, bool)` demonstrate?
options_id: Type assertion bisa dipakai untuk mengambil data yang hanya dimiliki satu tipe konkret
Interface menyimpan semua field semua implementer
Assertion selalu lebih baik daripada polymorphism
options_en: A type assertion can be used to access data that belongs only to one concrete type
An interface stores all fields from all implementers
`Shape` should have a `Radius()` method
Assertions are always better than polymorphism

quiz.question_id: Pernyataan mana yang paling tepat tentang type assertion di Go?
quiz.question_en: Which statement is most accurate about type assertions in Go?
options_id: Ini adalah cara mengonversi semua nilai antar tipe yang kompatibel
Ini hanya bisa dipakai pada pointer
Ini mengekstrak nilai konkret dari interface, bukan menggantikan desain interface yang baik
Ini selalu aman tanpa perlu pemeriksaan
options_en: It is the way to convert all values between compatible types
It can only be used on pointers
It extracts a concrete value from an interface, rather than replacing good interface design
It is always safe without checks
